public_rationale: A July 27, 2024 report said OpenAI could lose as much as $5 billion in 2024 and described Anthropic's expected spending as over $2.7 billion [e1]. A September 24, 2024 report described Anthropic's expected 2024 loss as over $2.7 billion [e2]. This reporting supports expectations of substantial losses, but does not establish Anthropic's specific loss outlook on a consistent accounting basis as of September 16, 2024 [e1] [e2]. Neither report establishes or directly refutes the asserted pricing strategy at either company, leaving the full claim unresolved [e1] [e2].
limitations: The sources are secondary reports of estimates, without underlying financial records or a consistent accounting definition [e1] [e2].
The July report describes Anthropic spending; the September report describes losses and postdates the claim [e1] [e2].
Neither report supplies direct evidence of pricing objectives or service-level profitability [e1] [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI and Anthropic are deeply unprofitable, with pricing designed to win customers rather than profit; Anthropic is on course to lose $2.7 billion in 2024.

statement.excerpt: These models are built by two companies that are deeply unprofitable (Anthropic is on course to lose $2.7 billion this year), and that have pricing designed to get more customers rather than make any kind of profit.

from_speaker: two companies that are deeply unprofitable
Anthropic is on course to lose $2.7 billion this year
pricing designed to get more customers
rather than make any kind of profit
our_interpretation: The two companies are OpenAI and Anthropic.
On course describes the financial outlook at publication, not a promise that the eventual audited result would equal exactly $2.7 billion.
Deeply unprofitable ordinarily means substantial company-wide losses relative to revenue.
The pricing clause asserts a growth-first pricing strategy. Losses alone cannot establish that intent or the absence of service-level profit.
The financial figures are treated as press estimates, consistent with the surrounding attribution to The Information. No GAAP or IFRS basis is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable contemporaneous reporting establishes substantial losses at both companies, an approximately $2.7 billion Anthropic loss outlook for 2024, and evidence that their pricing strategy prioritized customer acquisition over profit.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish profitability at either company, materially refute Anthropic's contemporaneous loss outlook, or directly refute the asserted pricing strategy.
